FN-U511DGG-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 253
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Donnie Chesteen
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/02/2024
Senate Bill 253 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the State Board
of Education to establish the new Workforce Pathways diploma at the K-12 level and would
increase the administrative and financial obligations of the State Department of Education, by an
undetermined amount, to develop and implement the Workforce Pathways curriculum for K-12
students pursuant to the provisions of this bill and to work with the local boards of education to
implement the workforce diploma pathway at the local level.
Further, this bill could increase the obligations of the Legislature paid from the Education Trust
Fund by an undetermined amount: (1) if the State Board of Education seeks additional funding
to construct, retrofit, and/or upgrade career and technical education centers throughout the state;
and (2) to provide additional funding for scholarships via the Alabama Community College
System’s Short-term Credential Scholarship Program. For FY 2025, the Governor’s introduced
budget appropriates $1,000,000 for the Short-term Credential Scholarship Program.

FN-U511DGG-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 253
Committee: Economic Development and Sponsor: Senator Donnie Chesteen
Tourism
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/15/2024
Senate Bill 253 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the State
Board of Education to establish the new Workforce Pathways diploma at the K-12 level.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative and financial obligations of the State
Board of Education, the State Department of Education, and the local boards of education by an
undetermined amount to develop and implement the Workforce Pathways curriculum for K-12
students pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Further, this bill provides that any increased obligations may be offset in whole or in part by
additional funding by the Legislature to construct, retrofit, or upgrade career and technical
education centers in the state.
Finally, this bill would provide that the Legislature may provide funding for the existing
Alabama Short-Term Credential Program. The Governor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025
appropriation includes $1 million for this program under the Alabama Community College
System.
